surprises.description: Verizon’s 406,000 postpaid phone net additions were far above the preview’s 150,000–200,000 range and its roughly 190,000 guidance-implied estimate. The result was also the strongest Q3 in five years.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Postpaid phone net additions surged 820% year-over-year to 406,000, the strongest Q3 in five years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Postpaid phone net adds: ~150k–200k”; the preview also said the guidance math implied “~190k+.”

surprises.description: Verizon raised its full-year postpaid phone net-adds guidance to 1.1–1.2 million, well above the preview’s existing 750,000–1 million range, even at its upper end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance raised to 1.1-1.2 million, more than 3x last year's result.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed full-year postpaid phone net adds guidance as “Upper half of 750k–1M.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.31 exceeded the preview’s $1.27 consensus and its estimated $1.28–$1.30 whisper range.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: $1.27”; the preview said the functional whisper was “~$1.28–$1.30.”

surprises.description: Verizon raised its full-year adjusted EPS growth outlook to 7%–7.5%, above the previous 6%–7% range the preview cited.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS growth guidance [raised] to 7%-7.5%, up from the prior 6%-7% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed adjusted EPS guidance as “$4.99–$5.04 (+6–7%).”

surprises.description: Verizon raised its full-year free-cash-flow growth outlook to nearly 12%, above the preview’s 9%–10% guidance range. Quarterly FCF was also exceptionally strong, at its highest level since 2020.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow reached $7.8 billion, the highest quarterly level since 2020 and up over 12% year-over-year,” leading to guidance “approaching 12%, up from 9%-10%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed full-year FCF guidance as “$21.9–$22.1B (+9–10%).”

surprises.description: Customer acquisition and retention costs fell much faster than the reductions cited in the preview for Q2, and reached their lowest levels in over three years without free lines.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Promotional cost of acquisition declined 41% and cost of retention fell 30% year-over-year,” reaching “the lowest acquisition and retention costs in over three years with no free lines.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 cost-to-acquire was down 15% year-over-year and cost-to-retain was down 17%.

surprises.description: Verizon unveiled a millimeter-wave fixed-wireless plan to add 10–15 million additional 1-gig premises beyond its fiber build, a quantified expansion of its high-speed broadband footprint not specified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new millimeter wave FWA solution using 1,700 MHz of spectrum aims to add an incremental 10-15 million 1-gig premises over the 40-50 million fiber build, targeting 50-65 million total high-speed premises medium-term.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for a “dated, resourced answer” to the competitive narrative and identified spectrum-position defense as a possible strategic response, but did not anticipate this specific FWA plan or added premises target.

surprises.description: Year-to-date buybacks had reached $4 billion, ahead of the $3.5 billion already completed that the preview cited. The reported total capital returns were also up 49% year-over-year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date capital returns reached $12.8 billion (up 49% year-over-year), including $8.8 billion in dividends and $4 billion in buybacks.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Share repurchases: Up to $4.5B ($3.5B done YTD).”
